claims.claim_text: On July 31, 2021 Lilium executed a term sheet with Brazilian airline Azul (Azul S.A. and Azul Linhas Aereas Brasileiras S.A.) for Azul to commit to purchase 220 Lilium Jets for an aggregate value of up to $1.0 billion, subject to certification. Azul Warrants were issued to Azul on October 22, 2021. In Jan 2023 and Dec 2023 the parties twice extended the deadline to finalize definitive agreements.

In 2022 U.S.-based operator Bristow Group Inc. selected the Lilium Jet to develop its eVTOL business line, obtaining rights to order up to 50 Lilium Jets, and intends to cooperate on maintenance for the Lilium Florida network.

Lilium has a partnership with Honeywell Aerospace and DENSO to co-develop and manufacture the electric motor for the Lilium Jet, and a separate development arrangement with Honeywell for the avionics system.

In October 2022 Lilium entered into a non-binding MOU with SAUDIA (Saudi Arabian Airlines Corporation), the national flag carrier of Saudi Arabia, contemplating the purchase of up to 100 Lilium Jets and yearly support services. SAUDIA is a state-owned non-US-listed entity.

Lilium has entered into a non-binding MOU with NetJets Inc., expecting NetJets to have the right to order up to 150 Lilium Jets for its fractional ownership program in the U.S. and Europe. NetJets is privately held (Berkshire Hathaway subsidiary).

As of the end of February 2024, Lilium has filed a total of 106 patent families (first filings) covering core aviation/eVTOL technologies including propulsion, energy management, power architecture, electric motors, and battery technology.

As of February 2024 Lilium has an order pipeline of 42 binding orders (sales agreements, production slot reservations, options) plus potential sales of up to 690 Lilium Jets across the U.S., U.K., Brazil, Spain, France, Italy, Benelux, Norway, Saudi Arabia, Cyprus, Israel, and the UAE. Distinctive product name 'Lilium Jet' is searchable across all SEC filings.

Lilium has a strategic collaboration with Bristow Group Inc. to support a 'Lilium Florida network' (US-based eVTOL passenger service network in Florida). Florida vertiport infrastructure for eVTOL would be expected to leave footprints in EPA FRS facility records or US-listed counterparty disclosures.
